Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) Second Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan II) (c. 600 AD)

OPENS Ch 19: FINAL-ARGUMENTS-FOR-RESURRECTION — the chapter's argumentation closes the systematic-treatise begun at Ch 14. The capstone-arguments synthesize: (1) creation-from-nothing (Ch 15:11); (2) elements-reconstituted (seed 14:19); (3) botanical-death-and-rebirth (seed 17:1 + 17:5); (4) Adamic-pairing (18:7 + 18:14); (5) prophetic-witness (Daniel 12 + Isaiah 26 + Ezekiel 37); (6) divine-justice-requires-judgment-of-deeds. The six-fold synthesis parallels the standard-Christian-patristic resurrection-apologetic structure: TERTULLIAN De Resurrectione Carnis §§1-63 (the most-extended Latin-Christian treatment); ORIGEN Contra Celsum 7.32-39 (the body-of-resurrection-debate); JUSTIN MARTYR Dialogue with Trypho 80; ATHENAGORAS De Resurrectione (the second-century systematic-treatise); GREGORY OF NYSSA De Anima et Resurrectione (the Cappadocian-philosophical-treatise). Meqabyan's distinctive feature: the six-fold-synthesis is PRESENTED AS REVELATION rather than philosophical-argumentation, preserving the prophetic-revelatory-genre.

Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) Second Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan II) (c. 600 AD)

**CHRIST-ALLUSION DEBATED** per Horovitz 1905 'von Christus nirgends die Rede' caveat (vv. 10-14): the chapter contains Christological-readable allusions ('the one who shall come from the throne of God to judge the living and the dead' — Apostles' Creed-resonant). Horovitz 1905 p. 196 explicitly noted that MEQABYAN NOWHERE EXPLICITLY NAMES CHRIST ('von Christus nirgends die Rede ist') — interpreting the text as deliberately OT-framed-and-pre-Christological. Tewahedo Christian reception reads passages like 2 Mq 19:10 as MESSIANIC-THROUGH-CHRISTIAN-OVERLAY: the 'one-who-shall-come' is recognized-as-Christ by Christian-readers but is doctrinally-unspecified in the text-as-written. Per CROSS_REFERENCE_APPENDIX §62: this verse is one of THREE INTERPRETIVE-FLAGGED MEQABYAN PASSAGES (Tier 3 reframing per SOURCES.md §7) — the Christological reading is fully-compatible with the text but not text-determined. The verse functions as a CHRISTIAN-READER-RECEPTION-FOCUS: where Christian-readers naturally see Christ-prophecy, while non-Christological readings remain textually-defensible (the eschatological-Judge could be God-Himself or an angelic-emissary in pre-Christian-Jewish literature — cf. Daniel 7:13-14).
